prds.title: Custom File Editor requirements
prds.problem: Own a distinct file extension and open it in a dedicated, editable Obsidian view.
prds.audience: Obsidian plugin authors and users of their generated plugin.
prds.goals: Own a distinct file extension and open it in a dedicated, editable Obsidian view.
prds.nonGoals: Operating-system file associations, binary parsing, domain-specific JSON schema, conflict-free multi-process editing.
prds.notes: Starter code provides the integration. Verify each authored requirement in an isolated real Obsidian vault before changing its status.

requirements.title: Create a custom document
requirements.acceptance: Given a disposable vault, when Create Custom document file runs, exactly one new .shellnote file is created with valid initial JSON and an associated dedicated view; an existing file is never overwritten.

requirements.title: Validated explicit save
requirements.acceptance: Given a custom document, editing keeps a per-view draft. Save accepts valid JSON without reformatting; invalid JSON never replaces the stored file. Opening an untouched or corrupt document does not rewrite it.

requirements.title: Incoming changes and uncertain saves
requirements.acceptance: Given an external change during drafting, saving is blocked until the user copies their draft and loads the incoming version. After a failed write, reopening and verifying the file is required before retrying.

requirements.title: Native lifecycle acceptance
requirements.acceptance: In a disposable Obsidian vault, verify create, explorer opening, file-menu opening, save, close, rename and disable/re-enable. Disabling removes registrations, closes owned modals and suppresses late callbacks without force-detaching leaves.

notes:
# Native integration starter

Own a distinct file extension and open it in a dedicated, editable Obsidian view.

Create a Custom document file from the command palette.
Open the .shellnote file from the explorer or its Open in Custom document context action.
Edit valid JSON and save. Invalid JSON is retained as a draft and never replaces the original file.
Change the extension and domain validator in the generated file contract.

Native tests in an isolated vault and domain-specific acceptance remain required. Portable JSON grants no execution or write authority.
